teaser.heading: The hand behind the needle.
teaser.lead: Born in Poland, trained in fine arts, and shaped by years designing creatures for video games — Tomasz brought a concept artist's eye to the tattoo machine. Once rooted in pure nordic linework, his hand has since darkened: characters, demons, and sketchy black inks now share the needle with runes.

chapters.title: Origin
chapters.body: Tomasz grew up in Poland, earned a master's in fine arts, and spent years as a concept artist in the video game industry — designing worlds, creatures, and characters before deciding the most honest canvas was skin. He transitioned fully to tattooing in 2019, carrying with him an illustrator's instinct for composition, weight, and darkness.

chapters.title: Craft
chapters.body: He keeps a deep archive of ready-to-use designs — characters, demons, rune compositions, sketchy black creatures — so if something calls to you, it can be on your skin the same day. For custom work, a conversation comes first. The imperfection in his line is not a flaw — it is the point. What looks raw on paper becomes alive on skin, and that roughness is exactly what makes each piece unrepeatable.

chapters.title: Speed
chapters.body: The sketchy style is fast by nature. Tomasz can complete a full back piece in a single session. His process: lay the base with magnums, then apply Angel Drops numbing cream before moving into the detail work. The machine keeps moving until the piece is done.

chapters.title: Influences
chapters.body: Old Norse rune-stones still live in the work, but so do demons. Creature design, dark fantasy illustration, and the rough energy of black-metal record sleeves pull at the needle alongside folk ornament and medieval woodcuts. The nordic thread hasn't broken — it's just tangled with something older and less holy.

chapters.title: Studio
chapters.body: Tomasz works out of Der Grimm Tattoo in Berlin. Private chair, by appointment only. No walk-ins. Sterile, single-use, and as quiet or talkative as you like it to be — he's equally comfortable with silence and with a six-hour conversation ranging from mythology to music to whatever you're obsessed with. He likes to learn from the people he tattoos.
